terms.meaning: A Python text-processing library, here used with an English language model.
The standard tool Python uses to install libraries.
A private folder of libraries kept separate from the rest of the computer.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Environment and library install
sections.what: Finds Python, creates and activates a virtual environment named venv if none exists, upgrades pip, installs the libraries from requirements.txt, and downloads the spaCy English model. Each step prints its progress.
sections.why: Likely reason: one script prepares everything the app needs on a new computer.
sections.watch_out: The install needs internet access and can take several minutes, and the script stops at the first failure.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Settings file, database, and next steps
sections.what: Copies the settings template to .env if no .env exists, runs the database init command, and prints next steps, including adding the OpenAI key.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app can start with almost no manual work, though the key must still be typed in.
sections.watch_out: An existing .env is left alone, so wrong or placeholder keys stay in place and only fail later when analysis runs.

summary: A first-time setup script for Mac and Linux that prepares Python, a virtual environment, the required libraries, the language model, the settings file, and the database.
purpose: Gets a new computer ready to run the app with one command.
why: Likely reason: setup has several steps that are easy to get wrong by hand.
how: Checks for Python, creates and activates a venv folder, upgrades pip, installs libraries from requirements, downloads the spaCy English model, copies the settings template if needed, and runs the database init command.
inputs: requirements.txt, .env.example, and the Python installed on the computer.
outputs: A venv folder, an installed set of libraries, a .env file, and an initialized database.
risks: Needs internet access, and installs can take minutes. The script stops at the first error, so a failed download leaves setup partly done. If .env already holds placeholder keys, setup still reports success and the AI steps fail later.
debug: Read the step number where the output stopped, such as step 5 for libraries or step 6 for the language model. Re-run the failing command by hand inside the venv.
